clue.text: Fly from despicable husband getting divorced

indicators.note: being divorced means being separated from a partner, so the husband's letter is parted from the word

parts.note: caddish means behaving like a cad, contemptible

explanation.surface: Someone flees a contemptible husband during a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb (flee) but is the noun: the caddis fly. 'getting divorced' removes H from CADDISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The caddis is a moth-like insect whose larvae live in streams, used by anglers as bait.

clue.text: It helps to clear the head

definitions.text: It helps to clear the head

parts.words: It helps to clear the head
parts.note: reads like a remedy for a fuzzy mind, but means a condition that leaves the scalp bare of hair

explanation.definitionFit: Alopecia is the medical term for hair loss, which clears hair from the head.

clue.text: Roman emperor to act on hearing embassy

parts.note: do means to act or perform

indicators.note: on hearing means the next word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a mission is a diplomatic embassy sent abroad

explanation.surface: An emperor resolves to take action once he hears from a delegation.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor's name is said doh-MISH-un, so its ending sounds like 'mission'.
explanation.definitionFit: Domitian ruled Rome from AD 81 to 96, the last of the Flavian dynasty.

clue.text: Sound of sleigh, and Santa Claus's last chuckle

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the words Santa Claus's

parts.note: a chuckle is a burst of laughter

explanation.surface: Sleigh bells jingle as Santa gives one final ho-ho-ho.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself a homophone: sleigh sounds like 'slay', and to slay is to slaughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken, sleigh is identical to slay, a verb for killing, and slaughter is wholesale killing.

clue.text: Licence for the Fool to retort with derisive mockery

indicators.note: to retort is to throw something back, so the word for the fool is turned round

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
to make sport of someone is to mock them, so sport is ridicule

explanation.surface: A jester is granted licence to answer back with scornful ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retort' turns SAP into PAS, followed by SPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is an official document licensing its holder to travel abroad.

clue.text: Hasten to insist

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the accelerator pedal hard speeds a car up, and taking a firm stand means refusing to yield.

clue.text: Nasty giants, black at heart

indicators.note: at heart means the answer sits in the middle of the words Nasty giants

explanation.surface: Wicked giants are described as having dark hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian means dark as the river Styx of the underworld, hence pitch black.

clue.text: Eventually get extra pay

explanation.definitionFit: Over time means in the long run, and the word also means wages for hours worked beyond normal ones.

clue.text: Shrub puts up tangled foliage — a hazard

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means writing the word from the bottom upward

parts.note: a mat is a dense tangled mass, as of weeds
a risk is a hazard or danger

explanation.surface: A bush raises a tangle of leaves that might trip someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamarisk is a feathery-leaved shrub that grows by coasts and in salty ground.

clue.text: Little bit of dirt found on creeper

definitions.text: Little bit of dirt found on creeper

parts.words: Little bit of dirt found on creeper
parts.note: suggests grime on a climbing plant, but the creeper is an earthworm and the dirt is soil it has passed

explanation.definitionFit: Worms leave small coiled heaps of excreted soil on lawns.

clue.text: Tease out my clue in school

indicators.note: teasing out untangles and rearranges threads, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A pupil is told to work out a puzzle clue in class.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyceum is a secondary school or place of instruction, after Aristotle's Lyceum in Athens.

clue.text: Mutant pathogen in shape of coin

indicators.note: a mutant has its genes altered, so the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A mutated germ turns up in the form of a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The British 50p and 20p coins are seven-sided.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-sided figure is the outline of the British 50p and 20p coins.

clue.text: Model is easy to make

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's model poses for a portrait, and in sport an easy catch or chance is called by the same word.

clue.text: Mathematical man losing his head — such a bore

indicators.note: losing a head means the opening letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a Cartesian is a follower of Descartes, the mathematician of Cartesian coordinates

explanation.surface: A mathematician gets decapitated, and what a dull fellow he was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tedious person but is a borehole, as in a well.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well is a borehole in which water rises under its own pressure.

clue.text: A British range? No

parts.note: the Pennines are the hill chain running down northern England

explanation.surface: Someone asks if this is a British mountain chain and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus the Pennines (northern England's hill chain) gives the Italian mountains; 'No' says the answer is not British.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain chain forming the spine of Italy, not Britain.

clue.text: I leave child in store

indicators.note: leave means the letter departs from the word for child

parts.note: bairn is a Scottish and northern word for a child

explanation.surface: A parent leaves a child in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a farm building used to store grain or hay.

clue.text: Loudly criticises living accommodation

explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer at a speaker or player, and military quarters are also called this.

clue.text: Bid for Soviet coin without head

parts.note: red was the colour and nickname of the Soviet communists

indicators.note: without head means the first letter of the coin is dropped

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian and Soviet currency unit

explanation.surface: Someone makes an offer for a Soviet coin missing its portrait side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bid' is a bridge call: doubling an opponent's double.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, redouble is a call that further doubles the scoring after an opponent's double.

clue.text: Blow a kiss

explanation.definitionFit: A peck is a sharp strike as with a beak, and also a quick light kiss.

clue.text: It's in one's interest to find him an office

definitions.text: It's in one's interest to find him an office

parts.words: It's in one's interest to find him an office
parts.note: reads as self-interest in finding someone a job, but describes a person given a post for political patronage

explanation.definitionFit: A placeman is someone appointed to a post as a reward for political support, serving a patron's interest.

clue.text: Make preparations to trap rattler

explanation.definitionFit: Spreading a mesh readies for a catch, and a castanet is a clicking instrument that rattles.

clue.text: The sort of animal that needs a trunk?

definitions.text: The sort of animal that needs a trunk?

parts.words: The sort of animal that needs a trunk?
parts.note: suggests an elephant with its trunk, but means a creature living in trees with trunks

explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal describes animals that live in trees, such as monkeys and squirrels.

clue.text: Mediocre batsman's record

explanation.definitionFit: Average means ordinary or middling, and in cricket a batsman's runs per dismissal is the statistic of the same name.

clue.text: Vast crowds run to the front of Greek island

indicators.note: moving to the front means this letter is shifted to the start of the word

parts.note: hordes are vast crowds
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Huge crowds rush to the front on a Greek holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is the largest of the Dodecanese islands, in the Aegean.

clue.text: Unyielding nature, yet it can be swayed

indicators.note: being swayed means being moved about, so these letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn might still be persuaded after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the stubborn can be swayed; 'be swayed' rearranges YET IT CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is stubborn persistence, a refusal to give way.

clue.text: Chap in Hackney can call in the doctors

indicators.note: to call in is to summon someone inside, so the doctors go into the word can

parts.note: taken as written
the BMA, the British Medical Association, is the doctors' professional body

explanation.surface: A man in an East London borough can summon medical help.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a London borough, but here it is a hackney carriage, the old name for a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabman drives a cab, originally a horse-drawn hackney carriage hired by passengers.

clue.text: It lends grace to manner, to be dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dancing gives elegance to a person's bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is a decoration that adds beauty to something.

clue.text: Key staff, perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key opens many locks, and a skeleton staff is a minimal workforce.

clue.text: Reason for, say, getting infested?

indicators.note: getting here means the word say takes a pest inside it, being invaded

parts.note: taken as written
infested hints at a nit, the louse egg that infests hair

explanation.surface: A person wonders why someone's hair is crawling with pests.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'infested' supplies the pest itself: a NIT gets inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanity means soundness of mind, the faculty of reason.
